tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Guidance in Sport

questions.question: Describe the four types of guidance used in sport and give a sporting example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Visual guidance: showing a skill through demonstration, e.g. a coach demonstrating a tennis serve. Verbal guidance: explaining a skill through instructions or cue words, e.g. "keep your eye on the ball" in cricket. Manual guidance: physically moving or supporting the performer, e.g. a coach guiding a beginner's arm through a javelin throw technique. Mechanical guidance: using equipment to support

questions.question: Explain why visual guidance is particularly effective for beginners in the cognitive stage of learning.
questions.correctAnswer: Visual guidance is most effective for beginners because they have no prior experience of the skill and need to see what the correct technique looks like. A demonstration provides a clear mental image of the movement that the beginner can copy. Beginners in the cognitive stage learn best by watching and imitating, as they do not yet have the motor programmes stored in long-term memory to understand

questions.question: What is the main disadvantage of manual guidance and how can a coach address this?
questions.correctAnswer: The main disadvantage of manual guidance is that the performer may become over-reliant on the physical support and struggle to perform the skill independently. A coach can address this by gradually reducing (fading) the manual support as the performer gains confidence and ability, eventually removing it completely so the performer can execute the skill unassisted.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Guidance in Sport

questions.question: A swimming coach uses a pull buoy with a beginner. Name the type of guidance and explain why it is appropriate.
questions.correctAnswer: This is mechanical guidance. The pull buoy is a piece of equipment that supports the swimmer's legs, keeping them buoyant. It is appropriate for a beginner because it allows them to focus on their arm pull technique without having to coordinate the leg kick simultaneously. It also provides safety by preventing the swimmer from sinking, building confidence in the water.

questions.question: Explain why verbal guidance is more effective for an elite performer than for a complete beginner.
questions.correctAnswer: Verbal guidance is more effective for elite performers because they already have well-established motor programmes and understand the basic technique. They only need small, specific verbal cues to fine-tune their performance (e.g. "hinge wrists earlier"). questions.question: Compare manual and mechanical guidance, explaining one similarity and two differences.
questions.correctAnswer: Similarity: Both manual and mechanical guidance provide physical support to help the performer experience the correct movement safely. Differences: (1) Manual guidance involves human physical contact (coach's hands), while mechanical guidance uses equipment/devices.
